title: Keep earlier leakage in the actual channel comparison
statement: A fewer-than-block-body Hamiltonian cannot directly rotate complementary deep-code words while exactly preserving that code. The supplied finite control uses shallower first-pair spaces on active blocks, with physical XX, representative Z and representative-to-representative ZZ pulses and a CNOT ladder. A trajectory-containing invariant subspace and exact Duhamel/CPTP contraction yield delta_internal<=2 integral sum_a[sum_(inactive j)|v_deep_aj|+sum_(pairs p in active blocks)|v_pair_ap|]^2 dt, uniformly on unknown inputs and arbitrary references. Previously leaked errors need not be reset before later gates. For the scalar hierarchy at fixed k>=2: width Theta(n), passive idle Omega(n^(2k-2)), serial X gate budget Theta(n^2) at fixed strength, two-qubit maximal support, no continuing reset during qualified internal operations. Greater depth improves idle life without automatically improving the gate budget. Noncommuting Hermitian noises are covered only when the required invariant subspaces can actually be acquired; the hierarchy supplies them for the stated commuting model.

All pulse duration/precision, external faults, calibration, source, measurement, decoding and terminal noise costs remain charged.
